regulations.title: Notify your local Public Health Unit before opening a food premises
regulations.summary: Before you start preparing, packaging, or selling food to the public in Ontario, you must notify your local public health unit and meet the structural and sanitation standards set out in the Food Premises Regulation. This applies to bakeries and packaged food producers, not just restaurants.
regulations.regulation_name: Health Protection and Promotion Act, R.S.O. 1990 - Ontario Regulation 493/17 (Food Premises)
regulations.authority: Ontario's local Public Health Units (under the Ministry of Health)
regulations.action_required: Submit a Notice of Intent to Operate a Food Premises to your local public health unit before opening, and make sure your facility layout meets O. Reg. 493/17 standards.
regulations.penalty_note: Operating a food premises without notifying the health unit can lead to compliance orders, fines, or closure until requirements are met.
regulations.source_name: Government of Ontario - Food Premises, O. Reg. 493/17

regulations.title: A Certified Food Handler must be on-site whenever food is prepared or sold
regulations.summary: Ontario law requires at least one certified food handler to be present at your premises during all hours that food is being prepared, packaged, or sold, so someone on your team needs to complete an approved food handler training course.
regulations.regulation_name: O. Reg. 493/17 (Food Premises) under the Health Protection and Promotion Act
regulations.action_required: Enroll at least one staff member in a Ministry-recognized food handler certification course before opening, and keep the certificate on file for inspections.
regulations.penalty_note: Missing certification can result in orders from the public health inspector and delay approval to operate.
regulations.source_name: Government of Ontario - Food Handler Training and Certification

regulations.title: Routine and pre-opening inspections by public health inspectors
regulations.summary: Public health inspectors inspect your facility before you open and periodically afterward, checking things like handwashing stations, food storage temperatures, and pest control, with inspection frequency based on risk level.
regulations.regulation_name: Health Protection and Promotion Act - inspection powers, and O. Reg. 493/17
regulations.action_required: Prepare your facility to meet O. Reg. 493/17 sanitation and food-safety standards and schedule a pre-opening inspection with your local health unit.
regulations.penalty_note: A failed inspection can block permit sign-off or result in a closure order until deficiencies are fixed.

regulations.title: Register to collect Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) on taxable food sales
regulations.summary: Most packaged and prepared food is taxable in Ontario, so once your revenue passes $30,000 over four consecutive calendar quarters you must register for a GST/HST account and start charging the 13% HST on qualifying sales.
regulations.regulation_name: Excise Tax Act - GST/HST provisions applying the Ontario HST rate
regulations.authority: Canada Revenue Agency (administers HST on behalf of Ontario)
regulations.action_required: Register for a Business Number and GST/HST account with the CRA before, or as soon as, you exceed the $30,000 small-supplier threshold.
regulations.penalty_note: Selling without required HST registration can lead to retroactive tax assessments, interest, and penalties.
regulations.source_name: Canada Revenue Agency - GST/HST for businesses

regulations.title: Register as a packaging producer under Ontario's Blue Box rules
regulations.summary: If you supply packaged food in Ontario and your business earns over $2 million a year, you're considered a 'producer' under Ontario's Blue Box regulation and must register with the Resource Productivity and Recovery Authority (RPRA) to fund and report on recycling your packaging.
regulations.regulation_name: Resource Recovery and Circular Economy Act, 2016 - O. Reg. 391/21 (Blue Box)
regulations.action_required: Check whether your revenue and packaging supply exceed the Blue Box thresholds, and if so, register with RPRA within 30 days of supplying packaged food in Ontario.
regulations.penalty_note: RPRA can pursue compliance orders and administrative penalties against producers that fail to register or report.
